title: Weakly Supervised Multi-Label Classification of Full-Text Scientific Papers

problem.claim: Classify full-text scientific papers into fine-grained, potentially multiple themes using only category descriptions rather than human-annotated training samples.

gap.claim: Prior weakly supervised paper-classification studies less often address large fine-grained multi-label spaces, full-text information, and structural signals across papers and within papers.

contributions.claim: FUTEX is a weakly supervised framework for classifying full-text scientific papers using cross-paper network structure and in-paper hierarchy structure.
The framework includes network-aware contrastive fine-tuning and hierarchy-aware aggregation modules for leveraging the two structural signals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two benchmark datasets reportedly show that FUTEX significantly outperforms competitive baselines.
FUTEX is reported to be on par with fully supervised classifiers trained with 1,000 to 60,000 ground-truth samples.

narrative_sequence.summary: Weakly supervised scientific paper classification uses category descriptions instead of human-annotated training samples.
Existing work gives less attention to fine-grained multi-label classification and use of full text.
Structural information from citation links and the hierarchy of sections and paragraphs should be exploited.
FUTEX combines cross-paper network structure and in-paper hierarchy structure through dedicated modules.
On two benchmark datasets, FUTEX reportedly outperforms competitive baselines and matches fully supervised classifiers trained on 1,000 to 60,000 labeled samples.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses both cross-paper citation structure and in-paper hierarchical structure.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary structural views may improve classification when document content alone is insufficient.

application.claim: For structured-document classification, model relationships among documents together with internal document organization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this combination is beneficial outside the reported benchmark setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, label definitions, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the weak-supervision procedure or model architecture in sufficient detail.
The abstract does not provide numerical results or variance estimates.
